doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: How the Alligator Bar song began
summary: De De tells how a Creole joke at the race track became a song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, when did that A-Log bar come about?

That came about when I was with the pass. We played somewhere on the race track. Out there, I think, I don't know. This fellow, I was singing a little Creole. We were talking to her. One word left, the other. He said, A-Log bar, and I said, A-Log bar, and that was the beginning of it. He started telling me, like, voices, you know, joking, joking ways, something like that. And I'd take this from the air and we made this song. That's how that started. As far as I can remember. That's how that started. The race track out there. The beginning of that. Then I just had in the voices and had in the voices and everybody wanted. Mm-hmm. Well, I want some special people, you know.
